feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis tried to attack its capital
entry.summary: Saudi Arabia on Saturday said that Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack Riyadh with a ballistic missile, the first time the Saudi capital has been targeted since the escalation in fighting with the Iran-backed rebels opened a new front in the Iran war.

entry.title: Ed Sheeran says situation in Gaza is 'catastrophic and unjustifiable' as he opens solo concert
entry.summary: Ed Sheeran opened a solo concert Saturday with comments about Gaza after controversy swirled around his tour and supporting acts withdrew in solidarity with opener Macklemore, who was dropped after making pro-Palestinian comments onstage.

entry.title: The new lines of southern Lebanon
entry.summary: The U.N. expanded the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon's mandate 20 years ago to include monitoring adherence to a ceasefire in fighting between Israel and Lebanon's Iran-backed Hezbollah — the militant group created in 1982 to counter a second Israeli invasion.

entry.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters denied access to White House following Trump ban
entry.summary: Three reporters were blocked from the White House grounds Saturday morning, a day after President Trump said CNN, Politico, and MS NOW would be banned for reporting "FICTION and LIES."

entry.title: Opinion: Remembering Annie Dillard, nature writer
entry.summary: With her 1974 book, "Pilgrim at Tinker Creek," Annie Dillard became the youngest woman to win the Pulitzer Prize. We take a moment to remember her and her work.

entry.title: Life in Kabul 5 years after the Taliban's return
entry.summary: Five years after the return of Taliban rule, NPR visited Kabul to see how Afghans are dealing with their new government's strict social restrictions.

entry.title: Betel nuts are a top mind-affecting substance. Now there's evidence of ancient use
entry.summary: New research on ancient human remains suggests the habitual usage of betel nuts, a plant seed with mind-affecting properties that is popular in parts of Asia despite the health risks it presents.

entry.title: Archaeologists are racing to save precious artifacts in Alaska after last year's storm
entry.summary: Last year, remnants of a typhoon damaged homes, infrastructure and an archaeological dig site. Now, archaeologists are trying to get as many objects out as possible before the next storm.

entry.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.

entry.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
entry.summary: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.
